governance.context: My Spindox internship covered Data Governance and Data Masking. This technical case study describes a separate personal proof of concept using synthetic data; its results do not describe Spindox systems or internal work.
governance.problem: Masking sensitive identifiers one field at a time can break joins, constraints and cross-system consistency. Moving unprotected data into development or analytics environments increases exposure.
governance.goal: Inventory and classify PII columns, apply consistent pseudonyms across related relational data and check that the protected dataset retains the intended technical properties.
governance.responsibility: I developed and documented the proof-of-concept repository: its CLI workflow, classification and masking rules, protected-database checks and automated tests. I do not describe internal company responsibilities or deliverables here.
governance.architecture: The local workflow generates synthetic data, inventories schemas and relationships, profiles and classifies fields, applies pseudonymization rules and validates the protected schemas. YAML policies are versioned; value mappings remain in memory during a batch.

decisions.heading: Consistency across tables
decisions.text: Deterministic pseudonyms use an external key, normalization and namespaces. Approved technical keys remain stable to preserve relationships. This also retains linkability: the process is pseudonymization, not anonymization.

decisions.heading: Reviewing ambiguity
decisions.text: Ambiguous classification does not trigger a guessed masking rule: execution requires an explicit decision. This adds manual work but makes the decision traceable.

results.label: Synthetic inventory
results.detail: 20 source and 20 protected tables; 109 columns inventoried and classified in the reference workload.

results.label: Documented checks
results.detail: The repository suite checks relationships, constraints, absence of schema drift and deterministic idempotence on the synthetic dataset.

governance.limits: Validation covers synthetic data only. It does not establish real-data detection accuracy, enterprise performance or legal compliance. Authentication, operational secret management and production observability remain future work.
governance.evidence: Counts and checks come from the personal proof-of-concept repository. They are not measurements of the Spindox internship; no company code, documents or data are included.
governance.repo_note: The repository is not currently publicly accessible. A code link will be added only when publication is appropriate.

dbt.context: A personal Data Engineering project using entirely synthetic e-commerce data, separate from the Spindox internship. The pipeline and dashboard are documented in a local repository.
dbt.problem: Late orders, subsequent corrections and columns introduced in later runs can create duplicates or inconsistent business metrics unless ingestion and transformations share explicit rules.
dbt.goal: Build repeatable loads, a dimensional model with an explicit grain and checks that make corrections and dashboard metrics verifiable.
dbt.responsibility: I built the synthetic generator, raw ingestion, dbt models, tests and Streamlit dashboard in the project repository. Business measures are calculated and checked in the marts, not recomputed in the interface.
dbt.architecture: Python generates reproducible CSVs and loads them into DuckDB with a transactional manifest. dbt organizes staging, current-version selection and dimensional marts. An order-line fact connects to customer, product and date dimensions; Streamlit reads a snapshot in read-only mode.

decisions.heading: Deterministic upsert
decisions.text: order_line_id is the stable key. The current version is selected by updated_at and, on a tie, a canonical payload comparison. This adds complexity but makes replay and arrival order irrelevant to the final state.

decisions.heading: Visible anomalies
decisions.text: Economically invalid rows remain in the fact but do not contribute to revenue. Missing dimension keys point to technical Unknown members, retaining the fact without claiming the data is complete.

results.label: Incremental load
results.detail: In the documented synthetic dataset, 10 new late rows and 5 corrections lead to 5,010 distinct order_line_id values, with no final duplicates.

results.label: Checks
results.detail: Documented tests show idempotent replay and parity between incremental and full-refresh results for the fact and dimensions.

dbt.limits: The workload is synthetic and local. It does not demonstrate behavior on real sources, production volumes or cloud platforms; the dashboard reads a snapshot and does not run ingestion on startup.
dbt.evidence: The project’s local repository documents the structure, checks and results. They are not attributed to a company environment.
dbt.repo_note: The repository is not currently publicly accessible. A code link will follow a publication review.

nosql.context: ITS course project by the Big Data NoSQL Gang group, developed in the former Databricks Community Edition. The recovered archive contains Bronze, Silver and Gold source notebooks, documentation and a visualization configuration; it contains neither CSV files nor execution outputs. “NoSQL” is the project name, not evidence that a NoSQL database was used.
nosql.problem: Prepare Inside Airbnb data for Amsterdam and Rio de Janeiro to analyze listings and reviews while keeping ingestion, normalization and analytical queries separate.
nosql.goal: Organize a Bronze/Silver/Gold pipeline and write queries for comparing the two cities. The group goal does not establish that the pipeline completed an end-to-end run.
nosql.responsibility: I was team leader and worked mainly on coordination and data ingestion. The exported Bronze notebook bears my name and documents that stage. Silver transformations, Gold queries and visualizations are described as group work: filenames alone do not prove authorship of individual cells.
nosql.architecture: The Bronze notebook reads four detailed listings and reviews CSVs from a Databricks volume, adds city and ingestion timestamp, and defines four Delta tables. The Silver notebook creates silver_listings with a UNION ALL of Amsterdam and Rio, selected columns, and type and price conversions. The documentation mentions silver_reviews, but its defining code is absent from the archive. The Gold notebook defines SQL views for counts and distributions; the IPYNB retains two chart configurations without exported values.

decisions.heading: CSV parsing
decisions.text: Bronze reads columns as strings and configures multiline input, quotes, escaping and PERMISSIVE mode for complex text fields. The documentation explains the move from summary to detailed datasets to retain ratings; the original data files are not in the archive.

decisions.heading: Layer separation
decisions.text: Silver preserves records with UNION ALL and defers analytical filtering to Gold. The documentation states that listings were not deduplicated; no exported check establishes ID uniqueness.

decisions.heading: Price comparability
decisions.text: The documentation distinguishes euros for Amsterdam from Brazilian reais for Rio and proposes city-specific comparisons. Some exported Gold queries do not apply the intended city filter, so the safeguard is not established for every visualization.

results.label: Source artifacts
results.detail: An ingestion notebook defining four Bronze tables, a notebook defining silver_listings, and a Gold notebook containing analytical views and queries are available.

results.label: Visualizations
results.detail: An IPYNB export preserves settings for two charts of counts by city and accommodation type. It contains neither chart data nor a snapshot of the final dashboard.

nosql.limits: Counts, performance and full-pipeline completion cannot be verified without datasets, run logs and outputs. The silver_reviews code is missing; some Gold queries depend on that table or contain errors and inconsistencies. The Databricks volume and catalog must be recreated for a new run. Publishing group artifacts requires a rights review and coauthor consent.
nosql.evidence: This case covers only the recovered original export and Samuel’s stated personal role. SQL definitions show technical intent, not successful execution of every cell. No metric or final dashboard is attributed to the project.
nosql.repo_note: Notebooks, datasets and dashboards remain private while data, licenses, contributions and group permissions are reviewed.
